messages:
raj: FYI the GH Actions run for infra/cluster-canary failed in a weird way — terraform step timed out acquiring the state lock and the subsequent helm upgrade picked up corrupted values.yaml. Anyone seen cache restoring helm values into the workspace before the deploy step?

deploy-bot: workflow 'infra-canary' failed on job 'apply' — exit code 1

raj: logs show `Error: timeout while acquiring state lock (context deadline exceeded)` from terraform, then helm stderr with parse errors in values.yaml. I can paste logs.

matt: ugh, this smells like an actions/cache + artifact race. If an older run restores a cached .helm/ values file into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, helm could see stale/incomplete file. Did we recently change the helm-values generation job?

raj: we did add a post-build cache for `.helm` to speed CI. The terraform backend is s3 + DynamoDB for locks. I also see this in the log around the timeouts:
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z [terraform]: waiting to acquire lock...
2026-03-18T14:12:28Z [terraform]: Error: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-18T14:12:30Z [helm]: Error: YAML parse error at line 12: unexpected token
```

julia: if the cache restore happened before terraform unlocked the state, parallel GH runs could both think they have workspace and try to apply. But you said DynamoDB lock was absent?

raj: I checked after the failure — no lock item present in the table. Strange. Also found partial `values.yaml` in the workspace that looks truncated (only 30 lines).

matt: Two hypotheses: 1) a concurrent run crashed while writing values artifact and cache restored the partial blob; 2) the actions/cache restore is restoring a packfile that gets overwritten by artifact upload mid-run. Either way, caching helm values is brittle. Quick mitigation: disable actions/cache for `.helm` and use explicit upload-artifact/download-artifact for generated values.

julia: agreed. For the terraform lock timeout, can you rerun the job with extra logging? Also `terraform force-unlock` can be used but be careful if another apply is truly in flight. We should add `terraform init -reconfigure` before `plan` to ensure backend config picks up correct S3 endpoint.

raj: starting a manual re-run now. If it fails again I'll force-unlock.

ci-bot: re-run triggered by @raj — workflow infra-canary #1427

matt: if re-run still fails, try canceling any older concurrent workflow in the same `concurrency` group. We should also tighten our GH Actions concurrency so only one apply runs for canary at a time: `concurrency: 
  group: infra-canary-apply
  cancel-in-progress: false`

julia: I'll open a tiny PR to: 1) remove actions/cache for .helm; 2) add upload-artifact for `generated/values.yaml`; 3) add `terraform init -reconfigure` and a more forgiving lock retry with exponential backoff.

raj: thanks — also adding a short TTL metric on the DynamoDB lock table to help detect stale locks; will follow up with monitoring rule. :thumbsup:

matt: one-off tip: if you see `Error: failed to read object` from S3 during restore, that's usually partial cache blob. `actions/cache` can corrupt on partial uploads. Artifacts are atomic and safer for small files.

raj: update — rerun succeeded after cancelling an older workflow and disabling cache restore in my local patch. Helm values now complete and terraform apply went through. Still going to merge julia's PR to be safe.

julia: PR opened: #487 — removes helm cache, adds artifact upload, adds init -reconfigure, and increases lock retry. Will add a changelog note so SRE knows about the concurrency change.

raj: perfect, closing the loop. we should also add a short playbook entry in docs/ops for ‘stuck terraform lock + corrupted helm values’ so oncall can triage faster.

matt: agreed. I'll add a 3-step runbook item tomorrow. :ok_hand:
